description:
Blind-spot `2026-05-02-155524` documented that the DuckDB community
datasketches extension (commit 2e38607, downloaded on-demand by
`INSTALL datasketches FROM community`) silently dropped the `theta`
and `frequent_items` families between PR #114 morning and the audit
later that day. Four sketch ops referencing `datasketch_theta` /
`datasketch_frequent_items` are still in
`benchbox/core/write_primitives/catalog/operations.yaml` and fail
end-to-end. CI does not currently exercise these aggregates beyond
loader unit tests.

Two work threads close the gap:

1. Fast smoke that fails the build if any planned-on family (`theta`,
   `frequent_items`, `cpc`, `req`, `kll`, `hll`) disappears from a
   freshly-installed extension.
2. Decision artifact (ADR) on vendoring vs HLL substitution. Current
   state of evidence: PR #182 already added CPC + REQ family ops, so
   HLL substitution is not the only path. Vendoring in
   `_binaries/datasketches/` gives version control but adds artifact
   tree weight.

anti_patterns.why: it is a CI-time check, not a unit test, and pulls a network resource (the community extension) on every run.

anti_patterns.dont: pin the community-extension commit by editing `pyproject.toml`
anti_patterns.why: the extension is loaded by DuckDB itself via `INSTALL ... FROM community`, not by uv. The ADR may choose vendoring as a separate mechanism.

preserves.behavior: Existing op definitions in `operations.yaml` are not removed -- the ADR may keep them and let the smoke gate the build instead.
PR #182 CPC + REQ family ops continue to load and run on DuckDB.
The smoke does not block the build for transient network failures fetching the extension -- network errors are reported but not fatal.

verifications.description: Smoke runs locally and reports per-family status

work_units.notes:
Connect to a fresh DuckDB, `INSTALL datasketches FROM community`,
then for each required family (`theta`, `frequent_items`, `cpc`,
`req`, `kll`, `hll`) call a representative function (e.g.
`SELECT datasketch_theta(1)`). Exit non-zero if any family raises
a Catalog Error. Print the resolved extension version (commit
hash) on every run so failures are diagnosable from CI logs alone.

Add a job to `.github/workflows/pr.yml` (or a new
`extension-smoke.yml`) that runs the script. Cache: do not cache
the extension download -- the whole point is to detect upstream
rebuilds. Job timeout: <2 min wall.
work_units.summary: Wire the smoke into a fast CI lane

work_units.notes:
Capture trade-offs: vendoring gives version pinning but adds
~5 MB to the artifact tree per platform; HLL fallback narrows
cross-engine sketch coverage but matches the Redshift ceiling
already documented. Decision criterion: how often does the
upstream community-extensions build actually drop a family? If
smoke catches drift in <1 month, fallback path is enough; if
drift is monthly, vendoring earns its weight.
work_units.summary: Author ADR: vendor `_binaries/datasketches/` vs accept HLL fallback

work_units.notes:
One-shot. Link the BenchBox smoke output and ask why the theta +
frequent-items families were dropped from the v1.3.2 build
artifact. No ongoing engagement; tracking the response can stay
in the ADR.
work_units.summary: File an upstream issue against duckdb-community-extensions if smoke confirms drift

work_units.notes:
Until the ADR's chosen path lands, mark the four affected ops
(`sketch_insert_theta_per_partition`, `sketch_insert_topk_per_shard`,
`sketch_query_theta_union_merge`, `sketch_query_topk_combine`) as
"blocked on upstream extension stability" with a link to the ADR.
